essence: The FlyVis connectome ends before the lobula projection neurons: 65 cell types x 721 columns, no LC/LPLC types (verified in the project on 16.09 via output_cell_types). The proposal adds a small trainable lobula layer on top of the frozen network. About 16-32 LC-like units would each pool retinotopically over the Tm/TmY and T4/T5 outputs with a nonlinearity, forming a low-dimensional bottleneck. The layer would be trained on an identity objective (pairwise or contrastive re-identification loss on train pairs) while FlyVis stays frozen. Cowley et al. 2024 showed that a 23-unit LC bottleneck between a visual front-end and a behaviour decoder, trained with 'knockout training' against genetic silencing, maps one-to-one onto real LC types and forms a distributed population code of object position, size and rotation. Xie et al. 2025 (Multi-Path Aggregation) predicted LC response profiles from whole-brain connectome topology and replaced a CNN with the predicted LC population for navigation and obstacle avoidance. An optional connectome-constrained variant restricts each unit's inputs to the type-to-LC connectivity from the optic-lobe connectome (FlyWire; Nern et al. 2025).
sources: 1) Cowley B.R., Calhoun A.J., Rangarajan N., Ireland E., Turner M.H., Pillow J.W., Murthy M., 'Mapping model units to visual neurons reveals population code for social behaviour', Nature 2024 (22 May 2024), https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07451-8, PMC11136655. 2) Xie J. et al., 'Visual Function Profiles via Multi-Path Aggregation Reveal Neuron-Level Responses in the Drosophila Brain', arXiv 2512.06934 (Dec 2025), https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.06934 (no code link found). 3) Lappalainen J. et al., 'Connectome-constrained networks predict neural activity across the fly visual system', Nature 2024, https://github.com/TuragaLab/flyvis. 4) Nern A. et al., male optic-lobe connectome, Nature 2025 (neuPrint optic-lobe dataset); FlyWire whole-brain connectome (Dorkenwald et al., Schlegel et al., Nature 2024). 5) Wu M. et al., 'Visual projection neurons in the Drosophila lobula link feature detection to distinct behavioral programs', eLife 2016 (LC feature selectivity).
relevance: Targets N11 (the fly used only where it is redundant, and the missing lobula stage) and N12 (uncalibrated or untrained readout). The plan already concluded that the readout must be trainable and must span all types. Today the signature is a fixed pooling (34 types x 19 macro-cells, mean) compared by cosine or by a linear head on |a-b|. A learned, low-dimensional, object-centric layer is the biologically motivated form of that readout and could raise the fly's identity signal above its 721-facet input. Currently the fly adds only +0.006 AP over the input on test, +0.010 at night. This matters for re-identification after occlusion (IDSw). Units tuned to small objects (LC11-like) or looming (LPLC2-like) would also serve C8 (births) and C7 (occlusion), but those are separate items.
novelty_overlap: Cowley et al. 2024: an LC bottleneck trained on behaviour. It is not connectome-constrained and does not use FlyVis. Xie et al. 2025: LC responses predicted from connectome topology and used in embodied navigation. Kuklev 2026: frozen FlyVis as a descriptor (without an LC layer). Training linear or MLP probes on a frozen network is standard practice. cannot_claim: (a) an LC-type bottleneck as an interpretable population readout (Cowley 2024); (b) deriving LC-like responses from the connectome for a downstream task (Xie 2025); (c) that our learned units correspond to real LC types. Without knockout or physiology data they are 'LC-like units', not LC11 or LC15. At most, a trainable lobula readout over frozen FlyVis for MOT re-identification can be reported, with information-matched and connectome-null controls.
author_results: Cowley et al. 2024. Data: 459 courtship sessions, 23 LC types silenced one at a time. Input: reconstructed visual experience of the male, last 10 frames (about 300 ms) at 30 Hz. The visual input is rendered from tracked body joints, so there is no real camera. Real LC responses to a fictive female were predicted with a noise-corrected R2 of about 0.35 (higher with a linear mapping; about 0.65 per a secondary summary) [uncertain]. LC11 size selectivity and LPLC2 looming responses were recovered. Held-out behaviour: forward velocity R2 about 0.5, lateral and angular about 0.15. Knockout training beat dropout and no-knockout controls in predicting mean behavioural changes. No single unit encodes one parameter, but linear combinations of the 23 units encode position, size and rotation. Xie et al. 2025: Pearson r = 0.84 +/- 0.12 for ON/OFF response profiles versus 0.33 +/- 0.59 for prior methods. Direction selectivity and complex-stimulus responses of LC neurons were also predicted. Replacing CNN modules with the predicted LC population gave successful navigation and obstacle avoidance in simulation (no quantitative tracking metric found). Neither paper uses a tracking benchmark.
measured_level: Neural-response fit (R2 or Pearson) and behaviour prediction (Cowley), response profiles and simulated navigation success (Xie). Nothing at pair AP, association links or HOTA/IDF1.
matched_control: Cowley: dropout and no-knockout networks as controls for the training scheme. There is no information-matched input baseline and no graph null, since the model is not connectome-based. Xie: a comparison against existing response-prediction methods. We did not find whether a degree-preserving topology null was run [uncertain]. For us, the controls must be (i) the identical head trained on the 721-facet input (hexin), (ii) the identical head on the rewired-connectome signatures (runs/fly_signatures_null already exists), (iii) the identical head on the current fixed pooling. In the connectome-constrained variant, add (iv) a random mask with the same sparsity.
conditions_breakdown: None in either paper (no night, overexposure, occlusion or density). For us, the dark/light strata from fly_matched_controls_v1 apply.
cost_here: The cheap version uses the existing cache only. Inputs: first_fly/last_fly (34 types x 19 macro-cells, 140 videos, 209,486 lives), with the same pairs as eval_fly_reid.py (train 78,385 pairs of which 10,845 positive, dev 31,390, test 32,178, val7 10,443). A bottleneck of 16-32 units takes type-wise weights x spatial pooling over 19 cells, then a nonlinearity, with a Siamese or contrastive loss. Training takes CPU or GPU minutes. The controls on hexin and on runs/fly_signatures_null use the same caches, so no rebuild is needed. The connectome-constrained mask needs a type-level synapse table (Tm/TmY/T4/T5 to LC/LPLC types) from neuPrint optic-lobe or the FlyWire codex. This is a small download, but the user must approve it first. A full-resolution variant (34 x 721 per life) needs a signature rebuild (about 18 GPU-hours summed, as the original build) and heavy storage (about 98 KB per life in float16, about 20 GB for all lives) [uncertain: rough estimate]. A macro-cell grid of about 61 cells is a compromise. Training the layer inside the online tracker, or end-to-end with FlyVis parameters, would take days of GPU and is not needed for the first answer.
expected_effect: Fly-alone AP (0.582 test) may rise with a trained bottleneck. The gain of the fly over the input is expected to stay small, 0 to +0.01 AP on test [uncertain: extrapolation, not measured], because the identical head on hexin will gain too. A learned metric on full vectors has already underperformed cosine (test 0.6632 for L_app_hexin_fly), which signals overfitting risk at this data size. A connectome-constrained mask might slightly widen the gap between the intact and rewired fly (currently +0.044 AP fly-alone, +0.003 over the input with the CI through zero). HOTA: no change is expected, since pair-AP gains of this size have not moved stitching HOTA (geometry-only 59.283 versus appearance 59.347, CI through zero).
risks: (1) Head capacity is a confound, so every comparison needs the identical architecture and training budget on input, intact fly and rewired fly. (2) Overfitting: with only 140 training videos, select hyperparameters on dev and report test and val7 once, with a video bootstrap. (3) Naming: units trained without knockout or physiology data must not be called LC11, LC15 and so on, only 'LC-like'. (4) The connectome mask requires an external data download, which needs user approval. (5) The cached input is macro-pooled, so fine retinotopy (where real LC dendrites integrate) is lost. A negative result at 19 cells does not rule out a lobula layer at full resolution. (6) Forbidden by the plan: transferring the sign from subsets to full runs, and presenting negative results as novelty. The detector stays frozen and is not affected, and FlyVis stays frozen in the cheap version.
attribution: Borrowed: the LC-type bottleneck and population-code view (Cowley et al. 2024); connectome-derived LC response profiles for downstream control (Xie et al. 2025); the connectivity data (Nern et al. 2025 or FlyWire); FlyVis (Lappalainen et al. 2024). Ours: a trainable lobula-like readout over the frozen per-track foveal FlyVis for MOT re-identification in BDD100K, with information-matched (hexin) and connectome-null controls, illumination strata, and propagation to stitching HOTA/IDF1.
